audit.title: Using Data Feeds on EVM Chains
audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured multi-language how-to for reading Chainlink Data Feeds, with complete, runnable Solidity and Python examples and strong primary-source linking. Its biggest GEO strength is structural clarity: no heading skips, tight sections, and copy-pasteable code with imports. Its biggest opportunity is discoverability and prior-resistance — three of five languages (Vyper, JavaScript, Golang) have no inline code (they link out or render a React widget), there is zero page-level structured metadata, and no symptom/error-phrased headings for the queries agents actually type ("latestRoundData returns 0", "stale price", "L2 sequencer check"). The honest verdict: solid reference prose that will be cited when retrieved, but underserved on metadata and query-coverage that drive retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased headings and a troubleshooting section
recommendations.where: new H2 near end + rename existing sections
recommendations.issue: no headings match "why does latestRoundData return 0 / stale price / L2 sequencer" queries
recommendations.change: add an H2 "Troubleshooting reading Data Feeds" with H3s phrased as questions: "Why is `latestRoundData` returning a stale or zero price?", "Do I need the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed?" — answer-first, linking to `/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds`.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by symptom; concept-titled prose loses retrieval the page already contains in a code comment.

recommendations.title: Surface the L2 sequencer requirement as body text, not a code comment
recommendations.issue: the L2 check lives only inside a Solidity comment block
recommendations.change: add a liftable sentence: "On L2 networks (Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Scroll), you must check the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed before trusting a feed answer."
recommendations.why: comment text is poorly chunked; an unretrieved answer here is unsafe, not merely incomplete.

recommendations.title: Add page-level structured metadata
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: [Solidity, Python, Vyper, JavaScript, Go]`, and a self-referencing canonical URL.
recommendations.why: structured metadata + visible freshness raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and parseability.

recommendations.title: Add inline JavaScript/web3.js code
recommendations.issue: only a `<LatestPrice client:idle ... />` widget renders — no liftable code
recommendations.change: include a complete web3.js snippet (import, HTTPProvider, ABI, `latestRoundData().call()`) mirroring the Python example.
recommendations.why: the widget is invisible to LLMs; a JS query cannot be answered from this page as served.

recommendations.title: Replace opaque "here" link text
recommendations.issue: "You can find it [here]" / "PriceConsumer example [here]" (3 opaque links, measured)
recommendations.change: use descriptive anchors: "the Vyper `AggregatorV3Interface.vy` interface" and "the `PriceConsumer.vy` example".
recommendations.why: descriptive anchor text is a stronger citation/relevance signal than "here".

recommendations.title: Lead the denomination section with the canonical formula
recommendations.issue: opens with soft framing before the method
recommendations.change: first sentence: "To derive BTC/EUR, divide the BTC/USD feed answer by the EUR/USD feed answer after scaling both to the same decimals."
recommendations.why: a self-contained, liftable rule outperforms diffuse explanation.

recommendations.title: Add a language/coverage comparison table
recommendations.issue: 0 tables (measured); on/offchain × language spread is prose-only
recommendations.change: a table with columns Language · On/Offchain · Library · Inline example (yes/link).
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract reasons and build justified multi-language answers.

recommendations.title: Add concrete feed specifics
recommendations.where: intro or a new "Feed properties" note
recommendations.issue: "several networks"; no decimals/heartbeat context in prose
recommendations.change: state e.g. "Price feed answers use `int256` with feed-specific `decimals` (commonly 8 for USD pairs)."
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

antiPatterns: Opaque link text ("here" ×3) in the Vyper section.
Vague quantifier "several networks" in the intro.
Critical L2-sequencer safety guidance confined to a code comment rather than retrievable prose.
JavaScript "example" is a render-time React widget with no source code in the served markdown.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; confirm this page is listed in it.

Site-level: no canonical/JSON-LD served on the `.md` endpoint — verify the HTML variant carries `TechArticle` schema and `dateModified`; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive metadata read.
Freshness cadence (a visible "last updated" date) is a site-template fix, not page-authorable here.
